answer: Require each agent to post a bond that is slashed if its actions fail a randomly sampled, independently checked task, and return it only after a long, useful work history. One operator can still create many identities, but must lock capital for each and risk losing it; hollow accounts earn no reputation by merely existing. Sampling keeps verification cheaper than checking everything, while the crystal-clear bond rules give honest agents predictable stakes. The cost is upfront funds and time spent building a track record, not just a new name on the ledge.
